To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(i) conceptual querying of XML is possible, (ii) it is useful and (iii) it is possible to integrate conceptual and syntactic XML querying in one unified query language
1) Conceptual query languages for XML are feasible.
(1) the conceptual querying approach is more powerful, (2) the MXS model provides the basis for the conceptual querying approach, and (3) the MXS approach is applicable to all XML query languages.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following three main topics: (1) an abstract model of XML Schemas (MXS), (2) the integration of this model into an XML query language, and (3) the evaluation of queries on XML data based on the MXS model.
the following questions: How to define a conceptual model of XML schemas? How can we use this conceptual model to define a new query language? How can we implement the query language efficiently?
the design of a conceptual query algebra for XML that can be integrated in a query processor.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MXS model provides an abstract and intuitive view of XML Schema that can be used as a basis for conceptual querying of complex XML documents.
our approach offers a new and more adequate high-level approach to query XML, beyond the purely syntactic approach to query XML trees.
the conceptual approach to querying XML is an important step forward and that it can and should be used to extend existing query languages such as XPath.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed an approach for conceptual querying of (XML) data that is based on a novel abstract model of (XML) schemas.
we have extended the XML query languages with the ability to query conceptual level information of XML Schema, thus providing new query capabilities and a more adequate way of querying XML.
the conceptual querying of XML is a promising approach that offers new and often more powerful query capabilities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is time for XML query languages to move beyond the syntactic querying of trees to conceptual querying of abstract models.
the conceptual level of XML schemas can be effectively used for querying XML documents.
the conceptual information in the XML schema can be used to improve the expressiveness and the efficiency of XML queries.
